advances: Concerns the depth of the entire fixed mixed measure restricted to one actual integer fiber. Ordinary depth computed from only that fiber is a different function.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The fibers follow by intersecting the five edges with the four integer levels. It suffices to consider halfspaces through $(2,t)$, since moving any containing halfspace's boundary to the point shrinks the captured set. With positive continuous coefficient write the cap as $x\ge t+a(z-2)$. The middle contribution is $4-t$. The two neighboring terms are the lengths $3-t+a$ and $2-t-a$ clipped to $[0,3]$ and $[0,2]$, respectively. Their sum is at least $\max(5-2t,0)$: if an upper saturation occurs its value is at least $2>5-2t$, and otherwise the two terms are their positive parts. Fiber zero contributes nonnegatively. For $t\le5/2$ take $a=t-3$, so the neighbor contributions are $0$ and $5-2t$, and $t-2a=6-t>2$. For $t\ge5/2$ take $a=2-t$, so both neighbor contributions vanish and $t-2a=3t-4>2$. These witnesses exclude fiber zero. An opposite continuous coefficient captures at least $t$ on the own fiber alone, above the obtained value. A purely integer cap through base two contains the whole own fiber and at least one neighbor, hence has mass at least six.

At $t=12/5,5/2,13/5$ the values are $9/5,3/2,7/5$, so $(3/2)^2<(9/5)(7/5)$. More generally for $A=3/2$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the two side values about $5/2$ are $A+3\varepsilon$ and $A-\varepsilon$. For every fixed real $p\ne0$, the average of their $p$th powers is $A^p+pA^{p-1}\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2)$. Raising to $1/p$ yields $A+\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2)$ for either sign of $p$. For $p=0$, averaging their logarithms yields $\log A+\varepsilon/A+O(\varepsilon^2)$, again giving a strict midpoint violation. Homogeneity preserves each failure under positive normalization.
statement: Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(3,0),(3,2),(2,4),(0,2)\}$ in coordinates $(z,x)$. Its integer fibers at $z=0,1,2,3$ are $[0,2],[0,3],[0,4],[0,2]$ and its mixed length is $11$. For $12/5\le t\le13/5$ the raw depth $f(t)$ of $(2,t)$ against all closed ambient halfspaces is $9-3t$ for $t\le5/2$ and $4-t$ for $t\ge5/2$. Both raw depth and its normalization by $11$ fail concavity for every finite real power mean on this single fiber.
title: Ambient mixed depth on one integer fiber fails every finite power mean
